content: Root cause: The bug was caused by the inability of the code to properly recognize and handle unknown transceiver types in the `ionic_get_module_info` function. When an unrecognized transceiver type was encountered, the code did not set appropriate values for the module type and EEPROM length, leading to potential issues when attempting to print or access transceiver data. The patch addresses this by ensuring that even for unknown types, the code sets a default type and length, allowing for better error reporting and handling.

Code statements:
```c
-	switch (xcvr->sprom[0]) {
-	case 0x03: /* SFP */
-	case 0x0D: /* QSFP */
-	case 0x11: /* QSFP28 */
-	default:
-		netdev_info(netdev, "unknown xcvr type 0x%02x\n",
-			    xcvr->sprom[0]);
```
